text:
Alex: FYI I'm seeing intermittent AUC drops in the judge ensemble after the q4 quantized bring-up. baseline run (fp16) AUC=0.78, some quant runs report 0.63 then recover. Root seems to be in the eval runner, not model weights?

Marta: ugh. can you paste the runner logs and the exact command you used to reproduce?

Alex: repro steps: checkout branch quant-onboard, run `pytest tests/eval_runner/test_integration.py::test_ensemble_report -k large` locally with --runslow. sometimes fails every run, sometimes passes. log snippet: 

```
2026-10-12T14:02:11Z runner INFO starting eval job job_id=jk_42
2026-10-12T14:02:12Z runner WARN lock timeout acquiring /tmp/eval-lock: owner=pid:12345
2026-10-12T14:02:12Z judge ERROR ensemble scoring incomplete, scored=2 expected=3
2026-10-12T14:02:12Z metrics INFO AUC calculation aborted (insufficient pairs)
```

Samir: the lock timeout is suspect. we've had a stale-lock race when parallel test runners share the same tmp dir. CI used to run with PYTEST_XDIST; did that change?

Jing: CI config note: we moved to ephemeral containers but the eval runner still uses a file-based global lock at /tmp/eval-lock per design to avoid concurrent KV cache writes. that should be namespace scoped but wasn't.

Rachel: is the lock causing the judge ensemble to skip the third judge model consistently? seems like the scoring pipeline treats missing model results as "skip" and recomputes AUC on fewer judges, yielding lower numbers.

Alex: yes — when a judge task times out due to lock, the runner marks it as failed and continues. our AUC implementation doesn't gate on full ensemble membership; it just uses whatever predictions available. that causes non-deterministic metric shifts.

Marta: short-term: can we make the metric compute only if all judges returned? i.e., guard AUC with an expected_count check. medium-term: fix locks to be per-job namespace.

Samir: agreed. quick patch: change eval/metrics/auc.py to raise IncompleteEnsembleError if results < expected and have the CI test assert error instead of silent low numbers. I'll open a PR.

Jing: ops: changing lock path to include $JOB_ID or use flock on a per-container socket would be better. ops-bot, can you schedule a quick infra task to ensure /tmp collides don't happen in CI?

ops-bot: @Jing scheduled job infra/2378 to add per-job lock namespace and switch to POSIX advisory locks. ETA 24h.

Alex: to help triage, here's a minimal repro script that intermittently fails in our env: 

```
# repro.sh
export JOB_ID=test-qq
python -m pytest tests/eval_runner/test_integration.py::test_ensemble_report -q
```
And the failing assertion from the test: 

```
E       AssertionError: AUC mismatch: expected >=0.75 but got 0.63 (scored on 2 judges)
```

Rachel: add a CI gating rule: if an eval run returns IncompleteEnsembleError, mark the run as flaky and don't promote model. That would prevent accidental promote with partial metrics.

Marta: good call. we'll also add a Prometheus metric `eval_ensemble_incomplete_total` so we can alert on >0.1% of runs.

Samir: PR 4321 opened with metric guard + test update. patch also logs the missing judges list.

Alex: verified locally after Samir's patch: when a lock causes skip, test now fails loudly with IncompleteEnsembleError. Once ops-bot infra change lands, we should see fewer occurrences.

Jing: CI wiring: need to ensure pytest-xdist and parallel CI job isolation use job-specific TMPDIR. I'll add to .circleci/config.yml and the docker entrypoint to set TMPDIR=$CI_WORKSPACE/tmp/$JOB_ID.

ci-bot: CI pipeline started for PR 4321 on branch quant-onboard (build 9112). Running integration tests.

Alex: post-mortem action items: (1) Samir's metric guard merged, (2) ops-bot infra task for per-job lock, (3) CI change to set TMPDIR per job, (4) add AUC gating rule to release pipeline. I'll own #4.

Marta: thanks Alex. can we also add a quick audit script that scans historical runs for `lock timeout` to estimate how many model promotions may have been impacted?

Samir: I can run `rg "lock timeout" ci-logs/ | wc -l` and post counts. will do after PR goes green.

Alex: great. ping me if you find any suspicious candidates to rollback. :thumbsup:

Rachel: noted for release checklist. thanks everyone.
